title: EXPLORE DIGITAL AFFILIATE MARKETING WITH CHATGPT
content:
Digital affiliate marketing means your business earns from recommending a product another person or company owns. That can remove the work of creating the product, but it also means your income depends on the product, company, and affiliate terms remaining useful to you.

The important decision is not simply whether affiliate marketing exists. It is whether there is a particular customer you can help and a particular kind of product that makes sense for you to recommend.

WHAT YOU ARE REALLY CHOOSING
Affiliate marketing is not a product category. It is a compensation relationship. The customer buys the vendor's product, and the vendor pays you when a qualifying transaction is attributed to you.

That makes "Who could I help make a useful buying decision?" more useful than beginning with "Which program pays the most?"

DEPENDENCIES TO NOTICE
You do not control the underlying product, checkout, refund policy, commission rules, or whether the program continues. Your exploration should produce both a customer/product direction and a list of current program facts that need verification.

EXAMPLE OF A SPECIFIC DIRECTION
Too broad: "I want to do affiliate marketing."
More useful: "I want to help beginner photographers choose editing software and earn referral commission from software I genuinely use or can evaluate."

The second direction tells you what customer and product category to investigate. It still does not prove that an appropriate affiliate program exists or that the audience will buy.

WHAT YOU ARE TESTING WITH CHATGPT

The goal is not to ask whether affiliate marketing "works." That question is too broad.

You are trying to discover what a digital-affiliate business would look like for YOU.

That includes what kinds of digital products you could credibly recommend, who would benefit from those recommendations, where your recommendations would naturally come from, what you would need to understand before recommending something, and whether you are comfortable depending on another company for the product and transaction.

A useful exploration should also expose the economics you would eventually need to verify in a real program: commission structure, attribution, refunds or reversals, payout conditions, prohibited methods, and whether compensation is one-time or recurring.

ChatGPT can help you identify those questions. Current program terms must come from the actual program.

CURRENT-TERMS CHECK

Affiliate relationships can also create disclosure obligations when you recommend products for compensation. In the United States, FTC guidance says material connections such as affiliate commissions should be disclosed clearly and conspicuously. The exact disclosure and advertising requirements that apply to your activity should be checked against current official guidance.

This guide can help you understand the business model. It cannot certify that a particular promotion, disclosure, or affiliate practice follows the rules that apply to you.

HOW TO USE THIS
Use the prompt below to turn this branch into your version of the business. Answer the questions honestly, ask for clarification when you need it, and do not treat external facts as verified just because ChatGPT mentions them.

WHAT THIS INTERVIEW SHOULD PRODUCE

By the end, you should have a specific digital-product category or type you could credibly recommend, a plausible customer who would value those recommendations, and a clear list of program facts that would need verification.

ChatGPT should distinguish your suitability for the business model from the quality of any particular affiliate program.

It should not invent commission rates, attribution rules, demand, or current program terms.

COPY & PASTE INTO CHATGPT

During the interview:
- Ask one question at a time unless a small group of tightly related questions is genuinely easier to answer together.
- Use my answers before deciding what to ask next. Do not run through a generic questionnaire when an answer makes a question irrelevant.
- If I say "I don't know," help me identify what I need to decide or research. Do not silently invent an answer for me.
- Explain unfamiliar business terms in plain language when they first become relevant.
- Separate assumptions from facts that require outside verification.
- Do not turn this into a marketing or customer-acquisition plan unless the purpose of this specific interview requires it.
- When you have enough information, stop interviewing me and give me the requested conclusion, including the important unknowns and next research questions.
Ask me one question at a time unless a small group of closely related questions would be easier to answer together. If I say I don't know, help me identify what I would need to decide or research instead of inventing an answer for me.

Interview me to explore a specific digital affiliate marketing direction. Learn who I could realistically serve, what digital products would be relevant to that audience, what knowledge, credibility, interests, or access I bring, and whether I actually want a recommendation-based business rather than product ownership.

Help me identify the program details I would need to research, including commission structure, attribution or cookie windows, refunds, recurring versus one-time commissions, restrictions, and dependence on the vendor. Do not assume current program terms or actual demand. Separate ideas from facts I need to verify independently.

End with a specific affiliate direction rather than the phrase "do affiliate marketing," plus a verification checklist.

NEXT → PDF 46 if the direction is clear; PDF 08 if you want another existing-digital model.

While interviewing me, follow these rules:

Do not begin by recommending affiliate programs. First determine the customer the user could help, the buying decision they could make easier, and the digital product category that naturally fits that customer.

If the user already has a vendor or program in mind, treat its commission, cookie window, recurring commission, restrictions, and other terms as unverified until current source material is checked.

Do not rank opportunities by commission alone. Keep product usefulness, audience fit, vendor dependence, attribution, refunds, and program durability visible.

At the end, give me:
- Customer/audience
- Digital product category
- Useful recommendation angle
- Type of affiliate relationship to investigate
- Program facts that must be verified
- Major dependencies
- Specific business-direction statement
